author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read DNSFilter Data Export queries: CSV files of up to 10,000 queries, one per line. DNSFilter writes them to an Amazon S3 bucket that a Sophos NG-SIEM S3 Ingest (customer-managed) integration reads. Queries flagged as threats go to the third-party alert schema, and all other queries go to DNS.
notes:
Setup:
- Data Export is a paid DNSFilter add-on.
- Point its Amazon S3 destination at a bucket a Sophos NG-SIEM S3 Ingest (customer-managed) integration reads.
- DNSFilter writes CSV files of up to 10,000 queries, one per line, with no header row, in the column order of its log data descriptions page.

Field mapping:
- Queries flagged as threats go to the third-party alert schema (blocked or allowed).
- All other queries go to DNS, which has no field for the policy decision or categories.

Made up in the samples:
- Samples follow the column order and the example exports DNSFilter publishes, with made-up values.

Testing:
- Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-13 (61 of 61 fields matched the emulator), and the parent's confirm string picked the same lines there.
- On 2026-10-14 each child also passed Run Test in a lab tenant as a separate parser under its parent.
- No built-in parser claimed these lines in 5 Run Tests.

Known gaps:
- The HTTP Event Collector destination sends the same data in a different shape that DNSFilter doesn't document, so it isn't covered.
